description: This plot illustrates the relationship between accuracy percentage and co-occurrence number for six different methods, identified in the legend as Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME. The x-axis is labeled "Co-occurrence Number" and utilizes a logarithmic scale with major tick marks labeled at 0, $10^1$, $10^2$, and $10^3$. The y-axis is labeled "ACC (%)", representing accuracy on a linear scale that begins at 60 and extends past 80, with major tick marks spaced at intervals of 5. All six methods are represented by solid lines connecting four distinct measurement points, and all exhibit a steady upward trend as the co-occurrence number increases. The "Base" method is represented by a black line with circle markers, starting at approximately 62.8% and rising to end at roughly 68.6%. The "FT" method is shown as a blue line with downward-pointing triangle markers, beginning near 64.0% and increasing to end at approximately 70.6%. The "IKE" method is depicted by a red line with upward-pointing triangle markers, starting at about 66.1% and growing to a final value around 72.4%. The "MEMIT" method, indicated by a purple line with pentagon markers, starts at approximately 68.1% and climbs to end near 74.8%. The "MEND" method is plotted as a brown line with diamond markers, beginning at roughly 68.9% and rising to approximately 76.9%. Finally, the "ROME" method is represented by a green line with square markers, starting at an initial value of about 73.2% and increasing to end at approximately 81.4%.
